cards.title: Introduction to Spring Boot Packaging
cards.content:
Spring Boot provides a convenient way to package your application into a self-contained executable archive, such as a JAR (Java Archive) or WAR (Web Archive).

By default, Spring Boot builds an executable JAR that includes your application classes, dependencies, and an embedded web server like Tomcat or Jetty.

cards.title: Spring Boot Build Plugins
cards.content:
To package your Spring Boot application, you use either Maven or Gradle plugins. These plugins are responsible for re-packaging your compiled code into the final executable format.

<plugin>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
</plugin>

Inside the Executable JAR
cards.content:
A Spring Boot fat JAR has a specific internal layout:

  • META-INF/ - Contains MANIFEST.MF pointing to the Launcher
  • org/springframework/boot/loader/ - Contains the boot loader classes
  • BOOT-INF/classes/ - Contains your application's compiled classes
  • BOOT-INF/lib/ - Contains your external dependency JARs

cards.title: Packaging as a WAR file
cards.content:
If you need to deploy your Spring Boot application to an external servlet container (like standalone Tomcat), you should package it as a WAR.

Steps required:

  1. Change packaging in build file to war.
  2. Extend SpringBootServletInitializer in your main class.
  3. Exclude the embedded servlet container dependency if necessary.

cards.title: Summary of Spring Boot Packaging
cards.content:
You have learned how Spring Boot handles packaging using executable JARs and WARs, the role of Maven and Gradle plugins, and the internal anatomy of a fat JAR.

This ensures your microservices are easily portable and ready to run in cloud environments!
